solution: Solution: Let $T_r$ be the $r$ -th term of $(x+a)^{15}$ , and set $t=\frac{a}{x}$ . Then $T_r=\binom{15}{r-1}x^{15}t^{r-1}$ up to the common factor $x^{15}$ . Given $T_{11}$ is the geometric mean of $T_8$ and $T_{12}$ , we have $T_{11}^{2}=T_8T_{12}$ . Thus $\left(\binom{15}{10}t^{10}\right)^2=\binom{15}{7}t^7\cdot\binom{15}{11}t^{11}$ . This gives $t^2=\frac{\binom{15}{7}\binom{15}{11}}{\binom{15}{10}^2}=\frac{75}{77}$ . The geometric mean condition uses the positive value, so $t=\sqrt{\frac{75}{77}}$ . Since $\left(\frac{7}{9}\right)^2 < t^2<1$ , we get $\frac{7}{9} < t<1$ . For consecutive terms, $\frac{T_{r+1}}{T_r}=\frac{16-r}{r}t$ . At $r=7$ , $\frac{T_8}{T_7}=\frac{9}{7}t>1$ because $t>\frac{7}{9}$ . At $r=8$ , $\frac{T_9}{T_8}=t<1$ . Since $\frac{16-r}{r}$ decreases as $r$ increases, the terms increase up to $T_8$ and then decrease. Therefore the greatest term is the $8^{\text{th}}$ term. © examsnet.com

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following orders are correct regarding their covalent character? i. $\mathrm{KF} < \mathrm{KI}$ ii. $\mathrm{LiF} < \mathrm{KF}$ iii. $\mathrm{SnCl}_2 < \mathrm{SnCl}_4$ iv. $\mathrm{NaCl} < \mathrm{CuCl}$ The correct option is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2024 Shift 1]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: According to Fajans' rules, covalent character increases with smaller cation size, higher cation charge, larger and more polarizable anion, and pseudo-noble gas configuration of the cation. (i) $\mathrm{KF} < \mathrm{KI}$ : Both have $\mathrm{K^+}$ , but $\mathrm{I^-}$ is larger and more polarizable than $\mathrm{F^-}$ , so $\mathrm{KI}$ is more covalent than $\mathrm{KF}$ . Thus, (i) is correct. (ii) $\mathrm{LiF} < \mathrm{KF}$ : $\mathrm{Li^+}$ is smaller than $\mathrm{K^+}$ , so $\mathrm{Li^+}$ has greater polarizing power and $\mathrm{LiF}$ is more covalent than $\mathrm{KF}$ . Thus, $\mathrm{LiF} < \mathrm{KF}$ is incorrect; the actual order is $\mathrm{LiF} > \mathrm{KF}$ . (iii) $\mathrm{SnCl}_2 < \mathrm{SnCl}_4$ : Sn is in $+2$ state in $\mathrm{SnCl}_2$ and $+4$ state in $\mathrm{SnCl}_4$ . The higher charge on $\mathrm{Sn^{4+}}$ gives greater polarizing power, so $\mathrm{SnCl}_4$ is more covalent than $\mathrm{SnCl}_2$ . Thus, (iii) is correct. (iv) $\mathrm{NaCl} < \mathrm{CuCl}$ : $\mathrm{Cu^+}$ is smaller and has a pseudo-noble gas $3d^{10}$ configuration, so it polarizes $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ more than $\mathrm{Na^+}$ does. Hence, $\mathrm{CuCl}$ is more covalent than $\mathrm{NaCl}$ . Thus, (iv) is correct. The correct orders are (i), (iii), and (iv) only, which is option i, iii, iv only . © examsnet.com
